Subject: Post-call: log handling & PII constraints — action items

Hi Alice / CareBridge security team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid discussion on telemetry and PII constraints. Quick recap from our side and the concrete next steps we committed to: 

Summary of customer asks (from the call)
- Minimize PII in request/response logs (names, SSNs, payment identifiers).
- Control/limit retention to 30 days for hosted logs; ability to opt for shorter retention windows.
- Provide an option to disable request/response logging on specific endpoints.
- Ensure headers with sensitive tokens (Authorization, Cookie) are never persisted in plain text; clarify trace-id handling (pseudonymize vs strip).
- Data residency: EU-only storage and processing for the pilot.

Immediate deliverables we discussed
1) Redacted sample of request/response logs demonstrating header + payload scrubbing (we'll provide a sanitized artifact).
2) Redaction spec describing rules for headers, payload fields, and trace identifiers (high level + regex examples).
3) Retention policy options and how to configure per-customer TTL.
4) SOC2 summary and evidence package for logging controls.

I'll follow up with the artifacts and a short technical note on how to disable request/response logs per-route. Can we target end-of-week for the sample artifacts?

Attachments: call-notes-20280411.pdf (internal call notes)

Next steps:
- Diego: assemble the scrubbed log example + redaction spec (deliver by 2028-04-14).
- Marissa: confirm per-route disable and any implications to caching/KV (owner).
- Monica: confirm SOC2 / evidence package and the EU residency plan.

Proposed follow-up: 30-min technical sync next week (suggest Tue 2028-04-17 10:00 CET) — please confirm availability.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Diego — thanks for the summary, this matches our notes. A couple of clarifications before we spin up the internal procurement thread: 

1) Trace IDs: we prefer pseudonymization for observability (so we can correlate across systems) rather than stripping. Can you confirm if Redwood supports deterministic hashing of trace identifiers (per-customer salt) so we can map them across requests but not reconstruct PII?

2) Retention: you mentioned "30 days" as a pilot default. Is that for hosted only, or can Dedicated/Private deployments be configured to shorter windows (7 days) or longer (365) as business needs change?

3) Disable logging: we need an API/route-level toggle (not just a global flag). Will that be auditable (i.e., will changes to the toggle generate an admin audit log)?

4) Third-party telemetry: confirm whether request/response logs are ever forwarded to downstream analytics providers or SIEMs by default. If we want to ingest into our SIEM, how is that exported and what controls exist?

Can you include an example of the sanitized log snippet and a one-page summary of the redaction approach? If we can get that by EOW that would be great — procurement is waiting for the technical artifacts.

Thanks,
Alice Wong
Head of Platform Security | CareBridge Health

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise technical response and the artifacts we've attached.

High-level summary (answers)
- Trace IDs: Redwood supports deterministic pseudonymization for trace identifiers. We compute an HMAC-SHA256 over the incoming trace value using a per-customer salt stored in the customer's KMS envelope. The output is truncated to 16 bytes and represented as hex. This allows correlation across requests without reconstructing the original ID. Recommended default: pseudonymize. Option to fully strip exists if required.

- Header scrubbing: we apply an allowlist/denylist model. Denylist (persistently removed or replaced) includes Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, X-Auth-Token. Allowlist includes common non-sensitive headers like Content-Type, User-Agent. We replace denied header values with a single token "<redacted>" in logs.

- Payload redaction: configurable field-level rules (regex-based) plus an NLP-based optional scrubber for free-text fields to remove names/SSNs. The redaction-spec.md (attached) has example regex rules and sample before/after pairs.

- Per-route disable: available. There are three mechanisms depending on deployment:
  * Hosted API: route-level config via the Console or API flag (x-rewood.logging = off) with change auditing captured in the admin audit log.
  * Dedicated: cluster config with route overrides; changes are auditable via the Console.
  * Private: customer-managed, we provide the config steps and audit schema.

- Retention windows: default hosted retention for request/response logs is 30 days. For Dedicated/Private deployments customers can set TTLs to 7/30/90/365 days. We can implement a custom TTL for the CareBridge pilot.

- Third-party forwarding: by default, Redwood does not forward raw request/response logs to third-party analytics. Exports to SIEM are opt-in; when enabled, exports respect the redaction rules and export destinations are configurable.

Attachments included:
- sample-scrubbed-log.json (a sanitized request/response pair demonstrating header replacement and pseudonymized trace IDs)
- redaction-spec.md (rules and regex examples)
- retention_policy.pdf (TTL options and how to configure)
- soc2-evidence.zip (summary index + pointers to signed report)
